title: Integrated multi-omics analysis indicates MARCO and ZBTB20 as candidate biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.
authors: Liu, Weihua; Ding, Tiantian; He, Keli; Han, Xu; Zhang, Cantong; Mei, Yifang
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学分析筛选RA与TB共病生物标志物MARCO和ZBTB20，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是疾病标志物而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients have a clearly increased possibility to develop tuberculosis (TB). However, the common molecular background, useful diagnostic molecules, and treatment-related targets of this comorbidity are still not sufficiently explained. We attempted to search the shared genetic factors and candidate drug targets for RA and TB by an integrated multi-omics way. METHODS: Bulk transcriptome data sets for RA and TB were obtained from Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were first performed to collect overlapped disease-related genes. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was then applied to select hub genes. External data sets, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) using clinical samples were used for validation. We also carried out immune infiltration analysis, gene set enrichment analyses, molecular docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, in order to describe possible function and treatment value of these genes. RESULTS: A total of 312 co-expressed genes common to RA and TB were obtained, and these genes were mainly gathered in immune and inflammatory processes. MARCO and ZBTB20 were kept as hub genes and showed acceptable diagnostic ability in RA (AUC = 0.839 and 0.795, respectively) and TB (AUC = 0.849 and 0.915, respectively). Single-cell results suggested their expression in T cells, B cells, and myeloid cell lineages, tightly correlated with immune infiltration and inflammatory signaling. Computational drug-repurposing analysis identified Tipifarnib as a candidate compound, and molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted potentially stable interactions with MARCO and ZBTB20. In the clinical cohort, MARCO expression was significantly higher in the RA-TB group than in healthy controls, whereas ZBTB20 did not differ significantly among the four groups. CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that MARCO and ZBTB20 may act as common diagnostic biomarkers for RA and TB. The clinical findings provide preliminary support for MARCO as a marker associated with RA-TB comorbidity, whereas the translational relevance of ZBTB20 requires further validation. These findings provide a molecular framework for further investigation of RA-TB comorbidity and may inform the future development of tissue-specific biomarkers and targeted interventions.
abstract_zh: 背景：类风湿关节炎（RA）患者发生结核病（TB）的可能性明显增加。然而，这种共病的共同分子背景、有用的诊断分子及治疗相关靶点仍未得到充分阐明。我们试图通过整合多组学方法，寻找RA和TB的共享遗传因素及候选药物靶点。方法：从基因表达综合数据库（GEO）获取RA和TB的批量转录组数据集。首先进行差异表达分析和加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA），以收集重叠的疾病相关基因。随后应用最小绝对收缩和选择算子（LASSO）回归筛选核心基因。使用外部数据集、单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）及临床样本的实时定量PCR（qRT-PCR）进行验证。我们还进行了免疫浸润分析、基因集富集分析、分子对接和100 ns分子动力学（MD）模拟，以描述这些基因的可能功能及治疗价值。结果：共获得312个RA和TB共有的共表达基因，这些基因主要富集于免疫和炎症过程。MARCO和ZBTB20被保留为核心基因，并在RA（AUC分别为0.839和0.795）和TB（AUC分别为0.849和0.915）中显示出可接受的诊断能力。单细胞结果提示它们在T细胞、B细胞和髓系细胞谱系中表达，与免疫浸润和炎症信号密切相关。计算药物重定位分析确定Tipifarnib为候选化合物，分子对接和分子动力学模拟预测其与MARCO和ZBTB20可能形成稳定相互作用。在临床队列中，RA-TB组的MARCO表达显著高于健康对照组，而ZBTB20在四组间无显著差异。结论：我们的研究表明，MARCO和ZBTB20可能作为RA和TB的常见诊断生物标志物。临床发现为MARCO作为与RA-TB共病相关的标志物提供了初步支持，而ZBTB20的转化相关性需进一步验证。这些发现为RA-TB共病的进一步研究提供了分子框架，并可能为未来开发组织特异性生物标志物和靶向干预措施提供参考。
